main_body: A flat sand-coloured ground patch (about 52x14 px) with speckled tan and brown dither, a small grey stone and a pink cross-shaped flower. It is a ground surface with no standing volume.
top_band: none; flat terrain texture with no top and front structure, which is correct for a ground tile
evidence: The candidate is a ground tile, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. There is no standing body, no front elevation and no receding side face. Reading it as terrain it is acceptable, so Part A passes.

style.evidence: The sand has about 4 tones (light cream, mid tan, darker ochre, a few brown flecks) in dithered blotches, so it avoids big flat fills. It has no outlines, which suits ground. Next to the grass and paving references, which have more steps and more tile-level detail such as tufts, per-stone highlights and shading, the sand is a bit simpler. The blotches are also fairly uniform and repetitive. The small stone and the pink flower add some interest, but they are sparse. It is a little thinner than the reference, though it reads as acceptable sand ground.
